title: Time complexity estimate
description: Estimates growth from loop nesting, known linear calls, recursion shape and project callees.
rationale: Always an estimate; input sizes are unknown.

title: Quadratic pattern
description: List searches, front insertions and string concatenation inside loops.
rationale: Typical sources of accidental quadratic time.

title: Allocation in hot loop
description: Materializing calls in loops; object creation or closures in nested loops.
rationale: Allocation pressure in frequently executed code.

title: Space complexity estimate
description: Collections growing in loops, arrays of non-constant size, recursion depth.
rationale: Always an estimate; input sizes are unknown.

title: Long method
description: Source lines of a callable.
rationale: Long callables are harder to read and test.

title: Large class
description: Lines and members of a type, over all of its parts.
rationale: A large type tends to collect several responsibilities.

title: Too many parameters
description: Parameter count of a callable; constructors have a separate limit because of dependency injection.
rationale: Long parameter lists are hard to call correctly.

title: Deep nesting
description: Nesting depth of branches, loops and guarded blocks; else-if chains stay flat.
rationale: Each level adds a condition the reader must hold in mind.

title: Placeholders
description: TODO, FIXME, HACK and XXX comments, and bodies that only throw not-implemented.
rationale: Marks unfinished work.

title: Dead code
description: Unreachable statements, unused locals, private members nothing refers to.
rationale: Code that never runs still has to be read.

title: Commented-out code
description: Line comments that end like statements.
rationale: Version control keeps history; disabled code is noise.

title: Empty catch
description: A catch block with no statements and no comment.
rationale: The failure is silently discarded.

title: Naming conventions
description: Types, methods and properties in PascalCase, interfaces start with I, parameters in camelCase; one-letter parameters of public methods.
rationale: Departures from .NET conventions slow reading. Formerly CC005.

title: Main sequence distance
description: Per module Ca, Ce, instability I, abstractness A and distance D (spec/metrics.md).
rationale: D near 1 means a module is rigid or useless.

title: Dependency cycles
description: Strongly connected components (Tarjan) in the module graph and the type graph.
rationale: Members of a cycle cannot be understood or changed separately.

title: Layer violations
description: Dependencies on layers that the configuration does not allow.
rationale: Layering was declared by the team and is being bypassed.

title: God class
description: Lanza and Marinescu detection strategy, high WMC, high ATFD, low TCC.
rationale: A class that knows and does too much.

title: Feature envy
description: A method using more data of one other type than of its own.
rationale: The method probably belongs to the other type.

title: Blast radius
description: Number of types reachable through reversed dependencies (spec/metrics.md).
rationale: Shows how far a change can propagate.

title: Impure function
description: A callable that returns a value and also writes state or performs I/O.
rationale: Cannot be reasoned about by substitution.

title: Side effect in lambda
description: A lambda passed to a higher-order function that changes outer variables.
rationale: The result depends on evaluation order.

title: Mutable state
description: Reassigned locals, mutable instance fields, settable properties.
rationale: Mutation makes data flow harder to follow.

title: Non-tail recursion
description: A self-call whose result is used further.
rationale: Cannot be turned into a loop by tail-call elimination.

title: Higher-order depth
description: Order of functions (data, functions, functions of functions) and lambda nesting.
rationale: High orders and nested lambdas are hard to follow.

title: Cyclomatic complexity
description: Decision points per callable (spec/metrics.md). Every value is a metric in facts; results are emitted above the limit.
rationale: More paths mean more tests and more room for mistakes.

title: Maintainability index
description: MI from Halstead volume, cyclomatic complexity and lines (spec/metrics.md).
rationale: A composite index; a hint, not a measurement of quality.

title: Duplication
description: Type-1 and type-2 token clones (rolling hash over normalized tokens).
rationale: A defect fixed in one copy stays in the others.

title: Test coverage
description: Line coverage from a Cobertura or LCOV report, per file.
rationale: Shows which files tests do not reach.

title: Encapsulation
description: Public mutable fields.
rationale: Hands a type's invariants to every caller.

title: Inheritance depth
description: Depth of inheritance tree (DIT).
rationale: Deep hierarchies are hard to understand and change.

title: Polymorphism
description: Several runtime type tests on project types in one callable.
rationale: Usually reimplements virtual dispatch.

title: Cohesion
description: LCOM4, groups of methods that share no state.
rationale: More than one group suggests a class that could be split.

title: Coupling
description: Coupling between objects (CBO), excluding the standard library.
rationale: Many dependencies mean many reasons to change.

title: Refused bequest
description: A subclass that overrides nothing and touches no inherited member.
rationale: Gains nothing from its base class.

title: Singleton
description: A class with only private constructors that exposes a static instance of itself.
rationale: Informational: recognizes the pattern; hidden global state is a cost.

title: Factory
description: A method that returns an abstraction and creates several of its concrete subtypes.
rationale: Informational: recognizes the pattern.

title: Strategy
description: A context class that receives one of several interchangeable implementations and delegates to it.
rationale: Informational: recognizes the pattern.

title: Observer
description: A type with events it raises, or a list of observers it notifies in a loop, with subscribe methods.
rationale: Informational: recognizes the pattern.

title: Decorator
description: A class that implements an abstraction, wraps an instance of the same abstraction and forwards to it.
rationale: Informational: recognizes the pattern.

title: Repository
description: A type named *Repository, or a collection-like API of get, add and remove over one entity.
rationale: Informational: recognizes the pattern.

title: Builder
description: Fluent methods that return the type itself plus a terminal Build-like method.
rationale: Informational: recognizes the pattern.

title: Service Locator
description: Resolving dependencies from a container inside business code.
rationale: Hides dependencies from the constructor.

title: Anemic Domain Model
description: A domain-named class with settable data and no behavior, while logic lives in services.
rationale: Behavior is separated from the data it belongs to.

title: Middle Man
description: A class that does almost nothing but forward to one collaborator, without a shared abstraction.
rationale: An extra hop with no value of its own.

title: Single Responsibility
description: Counts constructor dependencies of a class and the project modules it reaches into.
rationale: A class with many collaborators likely has several reasons to change.

title: Open/Closed
description: Finds the same enum or tag switched on in several places.
rationale: Adding a value then means editing every switch.

title: Liskov Substitution
description: An override or implementation whose body only throws not-supported or not-implemented.
rationale: Such a member cannot stand in for its base type.

title: Interface Segregation
description: Interfaces with many members, or whose implementers stub some of them.
rationale: Clients are forced to depend on members they do not use.

title: Dependency Inversion
description: Creating a project class that implements a project abstraction, outside composition roots and test classes (a class with test-framework attributes such as Fact, Theory, Test, TestMethod, TestCase).
rationale: The caller is bound to the concrete type.

title: Do not repeat yourself
description: Callables whose structure is identical up to local names and literals.
rationale: One piece of knowledge is encoded twice.

title: Keep it simple
description: Long boolean conditions and nested ternaries.
rationale: Too many decisions are packed into one expression.

title: You are not going to need it
description: Non-public abstractions with too few implementers, and unused private parameters.
rationale: Generality that nothing uses.

title: Law of Demeter
description: Call chains that walk through several distinct project types.
rationale: The caller is coupled to the internal structure of other types.

title: Hardcoded secret (heuristic)
description: String literals assigned to secret-like names, and literals shaped like known credentials.
rationale: Not a substitute for a secret scanner.

title: Insecure deserialization (heuristic)
description: Use of formatters that instantiate arbitrary types from input, or polymorphic type handling.
rationale: Heuristic by shape of code, no taint analysis.

title: SQL concatenation (heuristic)
description: SQL-looking text concatenated or interpolated with non-constant values.
rationale: Heuristic by shape of code, no taint analysis.

title: Goto
description: Uses of goto. Switch-case jumps are not flagged.
rationale: Breaks single-entry, single-exit structure of blocks.

title: Global state
description: Non-private static mutable fields and properties, module-level variables.
rationale: Acts as a hidden global.

title: Module size
description: Lines of code per module and per file.
rationale: Very large modules are hard to navigate.
